claims.summary: For a separable cost C(z)=Psi_1(|z_1|)+Psi_2(|z_2|) with Psi_j convex, nondecreasing, finite, Psi_j(0)=0, and N-point sets X,Y in [0,1]^2 whose counts in every cell Q of a grid of side delta are at least lambda|Q|: for every h in (0,1/2), min over matchings of sum_i C(X_i-Y_pi(i)) is at most sup over Lipschitz g of [int g d(mu_X-mu_Y) - (1-2h) lambda int C*(grad g) dx] + 2hN(Psi_1(delta/h)+Psi_2(delta/h)), mu_X, mu_Y the cell-smeared measures and C* the convex conjugate (possibly infinite).
claims.assessment: Working proof: finite matching duality (Proposition 4.3.2 of Talagrand's monograph), a Hopf-Lax semigroup inequality proved in the entry, Rademacher and Fubini, interpolation between the smeared measures. Deterministic; finite costs; one direction. The point-configuration, cell-smeared form of the standard dynamic duality bound (Benamou-Brenier; Bobkov-Gentil-Ledoux), sources recalled, not read.
claims.rationale: Turns a matching problem with any separable convex finite cost into a discrepancy bound penalized by the conjugate cost, the role the monograph's regularity step plays for Shor's theorem.
claims.next_action: Seek a converse up to constants, which would make the reduction an equivalence.

claims.summary: For alpha_1,alpha_2 in [1,infinity], L>=132, X i.i.d. uniform and Y evenly spread in [0,1]^2: if with probability tending to one D_N <= (L/2) sqrt(N log N), D_N the sup of int G d(mu_X-mu_Y) over Lipschitz G with int sum_j psi*_alpha_j(|d_j G|) dx <= 2 on the grid of side 1/ceil(32/s), s=L sqrt(log N/N), psi_alpha(t)=e^(t^alpha)-1 and psi_infinity(t)=N(t-1)_+, then with probability tending to one a matching has sum_i exp[(|X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)|/s)^alpha_j] <= 2N for finite alpha_j and max_i |X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)| <= 2s for alpha_j=infinity; for two i.i.d. samples with constants doubled.
claims.assessment: Working proof of the implication from lem:hopf-lax-matching-bound with h=1/4, a Chernoff bound for cell counts, the evenly spread cell count, and homogeneity of the convex penalty; the endpoint uses the finite cost N(t-1)_+. Conditional: no instance of its hypothesis is known.
claims.rationale: Reduces the ultimate matching conjecture at every admissible pair, endpoints included, with one universal constant, to one discrepancy bound of Ajtai-Komlos-Tusnady size.
claims.next_action: Test the reduced discrepancy statement against the Leighton-Shor lower-bound functions in an anisotropic tile.

claims.summary: There is L>=132 such that for every alpha_1,alpha_2 in [2,infinity] with 1/alpha_1+1/alpha_2=1/2, for X i.i.d. uniform and Y evenly spread in [0,1]^2, with probability tending to one every Lipschitz G with int sum_j psi*_alpha_j(|d_j G|) dx <= 2 (psi_alpha(t)=e^(t^alpha)-1, psi_infinity(t)=N(t-1)_+) has cell-averaged discrepancy int G d(mu_X-mu_Y) <= (L/2) sqrt(N log N), on the grid of side 1/ceil(32/s), s=L sqrt(log N/N).
claims.assessment: Conjecture stated to be tested; no evidence beyond consistency: it contains the gradient-at-most-one class at Ajtai-Komlos-Tusnady size, its penalty may be replaced by a weight at least linear at a factor e, and at (2,infinity) its class is a continuous counterpart of the monograph's Research Problem 17.2.2, open there. A reviewer heuristic suggests Leighton-Shor functions meet it at its threshold on the whole curve.
claims.rationale: Sufficient for the ultimate matching conjecture at every admissible pair with one universal constant, by cor:exponential-matching-discrepancy-reduction.
claims.next_action: Redo the Leighton-Shor lower bound for the penalized class in an anisotropic tile with explicit scale bookkeeping.
